definitions.explanation: A professional player of shogi or go who competes in title matches for a living.

examples.japanese: ⟦プロ→プロ：03871_puro⟧{棋士|きし}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: To become a professional shogi player.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{若|わか}く→若い：00823_wakai⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦プロ→プロ：03871_puro⟧{棋士|きし}になった。
examples.english: She became a professional player at a young age.

examples.japanese: {棋士|きし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{長時間|ちょうじかん}→長時間：10165_choujikan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{対局|たいきょく}→対局：17420_taikyoku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{深|ふか}い→深い：01211_fukai⟧⟦{集中力|しゅうちゅうりょく}→集中力：17614_shuuchuuryoku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{保|たも}つ→保つ：10134_tamotsu⟧。
examples.english: A professional player sustains deep concentration even over long matches.

notes:
Refers to a professional of shogi or go; which one is meant is determined by context. Go professionals are also called ⟦{囲碁|いご}→囲碁：18035_igo⟧{棋士|きし}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦プロ→プロ：03871_puro⟧{棋士|きし}: a professional shogi or go player
- {棋士|きし}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{対局|たいきょく}→対局：17420_taikyoku⟧: a match between professional players

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{騎士|きし}→騎士：14716_kishi⟧: a knight — a homophone written with different kanji
- ⟦{名人|めいじん}→名人：03753_meijin⟧: Meijin — a major shogi/go title, and by extension a grandmaster
